definition: Propensity means a natural, built-in tendency to behave in a certain way.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word propensity. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know propensity should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Volunteers learn on day one about the raccoon's propensity to unlatch cages, and they count noses twice before locking up.
A leaning is gentler than a propensity — a leaning nudges your choices, while a propensity reliably produces the same behavior again and again.
Obsession goes far beyond propensity — a propensity is a pattern others can predict, while an obsession is a pull its owner can no longer put down.

A tendency is the neutral, all-purpose word for any recurring pattern — machines, weather, and people all have them. A propensity is more pointed: a built-in, wired-in pull toward one behavior, the sort analysts track and price. Every propensity is a tendency; only the ingrained ones earn the stronger word.

Disposition names the overall cast of a nature — sunny, anxious, generous — the whole temperament at once. A propensity is narrower: one specific behavior a person or thing reliably produces, again and again. A cheerful disposition can still hide a propensity to gamble.

Propensity means a natural, built-in tendency to behave in a certain way.
Bridge engineers speak of certain alloys' propensity to crack in deep cold, and they design accordingly — as though the metal will do what it is built to do, not what the brochure hopes.
A propensity is a built-in tendency: behavior that flows from how a person, animal, or material is wired, not from a passing mood.
That is why the word turns up in reports and risk tables — a propensity is the pattern you predict and plan around.

Propensity is the analyst's word for a wired-in behavioral pattern — the kind that appears in scouting reports, risk tables, and case files, usually trailing 'for' or 'to.' Inclination (also in this unit) is softer and more personal: a leaning you might simply indulge.
Note a propensity in a report; confess an inclination over coffee.

Coach Alvarez kept index cards on every student, and Dmitri's card was mostly one note repeated.
The boy had a propensity for sacrificing his queen -- not now and then, but in nearly every game that turned tense.
It was not a habit he had learned from a book; it seemed wired into how he played, surfacing even after a month of drills designed to curb it.
Alvarez stopped trying to erase the pull and started building around it, teaching Dmitri to prepare positions where the sacrifice actually worked.
By the spring tournament, opponents who had counted the queen as safely traded discovered the drive was still there -- only now it arrived with a plan.
